reasons: Tests cover validation, fingerprinting, tiers and grounding with specific expected values.
Some counts are hardcoded and need manual updates when the catalogue changes.

terms.meaning: a check that must be true, otherwise the test fails
a short code computed from content that changes when the relevant content changes

sections.name: File setup, recent
sections.title: Test imports and a recent date
sections.what: Imports the test tools and the codebook, classification, tier and focus functions. Sets a date ten days ago that is used as a recent publication date in test signals.
sections.why: Likely reason: a recent date keeps the test signals inside the recent-days window.
sections.watch_out: The date is calculated when the tests start, so results can change if the window setting is changed.

sections.name: base (part 1)
sections.title: Tests for the default codebook and validation
sections.what: Checks that the built-in codebook has 30 solutions, four solutions that cannot be primary, seven themes, and a new project signal type. Also checks that validation rejects duplicate ids, fully excluded groups, branding, and fake built-in items. Checks that tier rules give the expected tiers, that focus scores are counted correctly, and that custom tier rules change results.
sections.why: These tests protect the rules that keep saved codebooks safe to use.
sections.watch_out: The counts of 30 solutions and 7 themes must be updated by hand if the supplied catalogue changes.

sections.name: base (part 2)
sections.title: Tests for the fingerprint, grounding and tier edits
sections.what: Checks that the fingerprint changes only when classification inputs change, and that a merge restores missing built-ins. Checks that a model result keeps only valid codebook ids, company names found in the signal, and new project quotes that appear word for word. Checks that editing only tier rules keeps the fingerprint the same.
sections.why: Likely reason: these tests ensure tier edits do not trigger re-classification while model output stays grounded.
sections.watch_out: The grounding test depends on the exact quote text in the sample signal, so editing that sample can make it fail for the wrong reason.

summary: Automated checks for the codebook rules: defaults, validation, fingerprinting, tiers, focus scoring and grounded classification.
purpose: Catches breaking changes in the rules that keep saved codebooks valid and classifications trustworthy.
why: Likely reason: the codebook has many rules that could break quietly if changed.
how: 1. Set up sample signal data. 2. Check default counts and validation. 3. Check that invalid edits are rejected. 4. Check the fingerprint changes only for classifier inputs. 5. Check tier results and focus scores. 6. Check that model output is grounded in the signal evidence.
inputs: The codebook, tier, store and classify functions, and the sample data written in the file.
outputs: A pass or fail result for each test, using the Node test runner.
risks: Expected counts such as 30 solutions and 7 themes are hardcoded, so a legitimate catalogue change fails the tests until they are updated.
debug: Run the codebook test file and read the failing assertion line. If a count test fails, compare with the supplied catalogue. If the fingerprint test fails, check which codebook field changed.
